mainEntity.name: Which JDK version should I install in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Install Java 21 LTS (Long-Term Support). It is the latest stable, production-recommended version as of 2026. LTS versions receive security updates and bug fixes for years, making them ideal for learning, development, and production. Avoid non-LTS versions (22, 23, 24) unless you specifically need a new preview feature.

mainEntity.name: Should I install Oracle JDK or OpenJDK?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most developers, OpenJDK is the best choice — it is 100% free, open-source, and functionally identical to Oracle JDK. Oracle JDK 21 is also free for personal, development, and production use under the NFTC license. Both are based on the same codebase. Beginners should use OpenJDK 21 from adoptium.net (Eclipse Temurin) for the simplest setup experience.

mainEntity.name: What is JAVA_HOME and why is it important?

acceptedAnswer.text: JAVA_HOME is an environment variable that points to the root directory of your JDK installation (e.g., C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21). Many tools like Maven, Gradle, Spring Boot, and Android Studio rely on JAVA_HOME to locate the JDK. Without it correctly set, these tools will fail to run or build your project. Always set JAVA_HOME after installing the JDK.

mainEntity.name: Which IDE is best for Java beginners in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition is the best IDE for Java beginners in 2026. It is free, powerful, and used by professional developers worldwide. It offers intelligent code completion, built-in debugger, refactoring tools, and excellent Spring Boot support. Eclipse is a good free alternative. VS Code is also popular but requires installing the Java Extension Pack separately.

mainEntity.name: How do I check if Java is installed correctly on my computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Terminal (Mac/Linux) or Command Prompt (Windows) and run: java -version. If Java is installed, you will see output like: java version '21.0.2' 2024-01-16 LTS. Also run: javac -version to confirm the compiler is available. If you get 'command not found' or an error, Java is not installed or the PATH is not configured correctly.

articleHeader.title: Java Installation Guide 2026
articleHeader.subtitle: A complete step-by-step guide to installing Java JDK 21 on Windows, macOS, and Linux — including JAVA_HOME setup, PATH configuration, IDE installation (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code), and running your first Java program.

blocks.text: Before you can write and run Java programs on your computer, you need to install the Java Development Kit (JDK). The JDK contains the Java compiler (javac), the Java runtime (java), and all tools needed to develop Java applications. Without the JDK, you cannot compile or run any Java code.

In this chapter, you will set up a complete Java development environment from scratch — covering all three major operating systems: Windows, macOS, and Linux (Ubuntu). By the end, you will have Java installed, your environment configured, and an IDE ready to write your first real Java program.

items.text: Java JDK 21 LTS + JAVA_HOME + PATH + IDE (IntelliJ IDEA / Eclipse / VS Code)
15–30 minutes depending on your internet speed and OS.
₹0 — everything in this guide is 100% free and open-source.

blocks.text: There are two components you need: the JDK (to write and compile Java) and an IDE (to write code efficiently with syntax highlighting, autocomplete, and debugging). Here is what we recommend in 2026:

Why Eclipse Temurin (OpenJDK)? It is the most popular free OpenJDK distribution, maintained by the Eclipse Foundation, and available for all major platforms with easy installers. It is used by millions of developers and is 100% GPL-licensed open source.
Follow these steps to install Java JDK 21 on Windows 10 or Windows 11. The process takes about 5 minutes.
Step 1 — Download JDK 21

items.html: Go to adoptium.net (Eclipse Temurin) or oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads
Select: Version = 21 (LTS) → Operating System = Windows → Architecture = x64
Download the .msi installer file (e.g., OpenJDK21U-jdk_x64_windows_hotspot_21.0.x.msi)

blocks.text: Step 2 — Run the Installer

items.html: Double-click the downloaded .msi file to launch the installer wizard.
Click Next → keep the default installation path (C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.x.x.x-hotspot\) → Click Install.
✅ Important: On the feature selection screen, make sure "Set JAVA_HOME variable" and "Add to PATH" checkboxes are enabled. The Temurin installer can set these automatically.
Click Finish when installation is complete.

blocks.text: If the installer did not set JAVA_HOME automatically, or if you need to switch between multiple JDK versions, here is how to set it manually on Windows.
Method 1 — Using System Properties GUI

items.html: Press Win + S → Search "Environment Variables" → Click "Edit the system environment variables"

Under System variables → Click "New"
Variable name: JAVA_HOME | Variable value: C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-21.0.2.13-hotspot → Click OK
In System variables → Find and select Path → Click "Edit" → Click "New" → Add: %JAVA_HOME%\bin → Click OK on all windows.
Restart Command Prompt (close and reopen) → run java -version to confirm.

sections.title: Java IDE — Which One to Choose?

blocks.text: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) makes writing Java dramatically easier — it provides syntax highlighting, autocomplete, real-time error detection, built-in debugger, project management, and Git integration. While you can write Java in any text editor + terminal, a good IDE can easily 10x your productivity.

Our recommendation: Start with IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition — it is free, used professionally, and has excellent Java and Spring Boot support. Once you are comfortable, the Community edition will serve you through your entire Java learning journey.
IntelliJ IDEA by JetBrains is the world's most popular Java IDE. The Community Edition is completely free and covers all Java basics, OOP, Maven, Gradle, and unit testing. Here is how to install it:

items.html: Step 1: Go to jetbrains.com/idea/download
Step 2: Choose your OS (Windows / macOS / Linux) → Under Community section → Click Download
Step 3 (Windows): Run the .exe installer → Check "Add to PATH", "Create desktop shortcut", and ".java association" → Click Install.
Step 3 (macOS): Open the .dmg file → Drag IntelliJ IDEA CE to the Applications folder.
Step 3 (Linux): Extract the .tar.gz → Navigate to bin/ → Run ./idea.sh → Optionally create a desktop entry via Tools → Create Desktop Entry.
Step 4: Launch IntelliJ IDEA → Select "Do not import settings" → Choose a theme (Darcula dark or IntelliJ light) → Click Start using IntelliJ IDEA.

blocks.text: Create & Run Your First Java Project in IntelliJ

items.html: 1. Click "New Project" → Select Java → Set JDK = 21 (IntelliJ auto-detects installed JDK) → Click Next
2. Check "Create project from template" → Select "Command Line App" → Click Next
3. Project name: JavaFirstProject → Base package: com.techsustainify → Click Finish
4. IntelliJ creates a Main.java file → Inside main() method, add: System.out.println("Hello from IntelliJ!");
5. Click the ▶ Run button (or press Shift + F10) → See output in the Run panel at the bottom.

blocks.text: Eclipse IDE is a powerful, free, open-source Java IDE that has been the industry standard in enterprise Java development for decades. It is especially popular in large organizations and academic institutions.

items.html: Step 1: Go to eclipse.org/downloads → Click "Download x86_64" to get the Eclipse Installer.
Step 2: Run the Eclipse Installer → Select "Eclipse IDE for Java Developers" from the package list.
Step 3: In the installer: Java JVM → select your JDK 21 installation path → Choose installation folder → Click Install.
Step 4: Accept the license agreement → Wait for installation to complete → Click Launch.
Step 5: Choose a workspace folder (e.g., C:\Users\YourName\eclipse-workspace) → Click Launch.

blocks.text: Create First Java Program in Eclipse

items.html: File → New → Java Project → Name: JavaFirstProject → JRE: JavaSE-21 → Finish
Right-click src folder → New → Class → Name: HelloWorld → Check "public static void main" → Finish
Inside main(): add System.out.println("Hello from Eclipse!");
Press Ctrl + F11 (or Run → Run) → Output appears in the Console panel.

sections.title: Install VS Code for Java Development

blocks.text: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a lightweight, fast, free code editor from Microsoft. With the Java Extension Pack, it becomes a capable Java IDE. It is a great choice if you prefer a lighter tool or already use VS Code for other languages.

items.html: Step 1: Download VS Code from code.visualstudio.com → Install for your OS.
Step 2: Open VS Code → Press Ctrl + Shift + X to open Extensions panel.

Step 3: Search for "Extension Pack for Java" (by Microsoft) → Click Install. This installs 6 extensions: Language Support for Java, Debugger for Java, Test Runner, Maven, Project Manager, and IntelliCode.
Step 4: VS Code will auto-detect your JDK 21 installation via JAVA_HOME. If not detected: Ctrl + Shift + P → "Java: Configure Java Runtime" → Add JDK path manually.
Step 5: Ctrl + Shift + P → "Java: Create Java Project" → No build tools → Choose a folder → Enter project name → VS Code creates the project structure.

Installation issues are common — especially around PATH and JAVA_HOME configuration. Here are the most frequent errors beginners face and exactly how to fix them.

rows: 'java' is not recognized as an internal or external command
Java is not added to PATH (Windows)
Add %JAVA_HOME%\bin to System PATH → Restart CMD
Add export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc → source it
'javac' is not recognized / javac: command not found
JRE installed instead of JDK (no compiler)
Uninstall JRE → Install full JDK 21 instead
Set JAVA_HOME to JDK root directory (not /bin)
Change project SDK to Java 21 in IDE settings
Compiled with newer Java, running on older JVM
Update JVM to match or exceed compile-time Java version
Old Java version still active on PATH
Use update-alternatives (Linux) or uninstall old version (Windows)

blocks.text: These questions are commonly asked in Java fresher interviews related to environment setup and Java toolchain knowledge.

items.q: Q1. What is JAVA_HOME and why is it needed?
items.a: JAVA_HOME is an environment variable that points to the root directory of your JDK installation (e.g., C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21 on Windows or /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64 on Linux). It is required by build tools like Maven, Gradle, Ant, and many frameworks like Spring Boot and Android Studio. Without JAVA_HOME correctly set, these tools cannot locate the JDK and will fail to build your project.

items.q: Q2. What is the difference between installing JRE and JDK?
items.a: JRE (Java Runtime Environment) contains only what is needed to RUN Java applications — the JVM and standard class libraries. It does NOT include the Java compiler (javac). JDK (Java Development Kit) is a superset of JRE — it includes everything in JRE plus the compiler (javac), debugger (jdb), documentation generator (javadoc), and other developer tools. As a developer, you always install the JDK.

items.q: Q3. What is the command to compile a Java file and run it?
items.a: To compile: javac HelloWorld.java — this produces HelloWorld.class bytecode. To run: java HelloWorld — note: no .class extension, just the class name. The java command starts the JVM, which loads and executes the HelloWorld.class file. Both commands must be run from the directory containing the .java / .class files, or the classpath must include that directory.

items.q: Q4. What is OpenJDK? How is it different from Oracle JDK?
items.a: OpenJDK is the open-source, community-maintained reference implementation of Java, licensed under GPL. Oracle JDK is Oracle's build of the same codebase with some additional tools. Since Java 11, Oracle JDK and OpenJDK are nearly identical in functionality. Oracle JDK 21 is free for development and production under the NFTC license. OpenJDK distributions like Eclipse Temurin are fully GPL-licensed and completely free. Most developers prefer OpenJDK in 2026.

items.q: Q5. What does 'LTS' mean in Java 21 LTS?
items.a: LTS stands for Long-Term Support. LTS versions of Java (8, 11, 17, 21) receive security patches and bug fixes for a long period — typically 5–10+ years for Oracle JDK. Non-LTS versions (22, 23, 24) get support only for 6 months before the next version is released. For production systems and learning, always prefer LTS versions. Java 21 LTS is the recommended version in 2026.

items.q: Q6. How do you check which Java version is installed on your system?
items.a: Open Terminal (Mac/Linux) or Command Prompt (Windows) and run: java -version. This shows the JRE version. Run javac -version to check the JDK compiler version. To see all installed JDK paths on Linux, run: update-alternatives --list java. On macOS, run: /usr/libexec/java_home -V to list all installed JVMs.

items.q: Q7. What is the PATH environment variable and why must the JDK bin be added to it?
items.a: PATH is a system environment variable that tells the OS where to look for executable programs. When you type 'java' or 'javac' in the terminal, the OS searches every directory listed in PATH for those executables. The JDK bin directory contains java.exe, javac.exe, javadoc.exe, etc. Adding the JDK bin to PATH lets you run these commands from any directory without specifying their full path.

items.q: Q8. What is Eclipse Temurin? Why is it recommended in 2026?
items.a: Eclipse Temurin is a free, open-source JDK distribution maintained by the Eclipse Foundation's Adoptium working group. It is a production-ready, fully GPL-licensed build of OpenJDK available for Windows, macOS, and Linux in both installer and zip formats. It is recommended in 2026 because it is vendor-neutral, regularly updated, certified against the Java TCK, and has no commercial licensing complexities — making it the safe default choice for developers worldwide.

blocks.text: Test your understanding of Java installation and environment setup with these practice questions.

items.q: 1. You installed Java but 'java' command gives 'command not found'. What are the two most likely causes?
items.a: Cause 1: The JDK bin directory is not added to the system PATH variable. Fix: Add %JAVA_HOME%\bin (Windows) or $JAVA_HOME/bin (Mac/Linux) to PATH and restart the terminal. Cause 2: JAVA_HOME is not set or points to the wrong directory. Fix: Set JAVA_HOME to the root of the JDK installation (not the /bin subdirectory). Always restart/re-source the terminal after making environment variable changes.

items.q: 2. What is the correct value for JAVA_HOME if Java is installed at C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.2?
items.a: JAVA_HOME = C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.2. This is the root directory of the JDK — NOT C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.2\bin. JAVA_HOME points to the root, and then the PATH entry adds \bin to it: %JAVA_HOME%\bin. This separation makes it easy to update the JDK version by just changing JAVA_HOME in one place.

items.q: 3. Why does 'javac' command work but 'java' command give an error (or vice versa)?
items.a: 'javac' works but 'java' fails: This means the JDK compiler is on PATH but the JVM is not — unlikely but possible with manual PATH configuration. More commonly, there are two Java installations conflicting. 'java' works but 'javac' fails: This means only JRE is installed (not full JDK) — JRE has java.exe but not javac.exe. Fix: Uninstall JRE-only installation and install the full JDK 21.

items.q: 4. What is the file extension of compiled Java bytecode? Where is it stored?
items.a: Compiled Java bytecode files have the .class extension. When you compile HelloWorld.java using javac HelloWorld.java, it generates HelloWorld.class in the same directory by default. You can specify a different output directory with the -d flag: javac -d ./out HelloWorld.java — this puts HelloWorld.class in the ./out folder. The .class file is platform-neutral bytecode that the JVM executes.

items.q: 5. On Linux, you have Java 11 and Java 21 installed. How do you switch the active version to Java 21?
items.a: Run: sudo update-alternatives --config java. This displays a numbered list of all installed Java versions. Enter the number corresponding to Java 21 and press Enter. Verify: java -version. Also update JAVA_HOME in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to point to the Java 21 path, then run source ~/.bashrc to apply.

items.q: 6. What is the difference between 'java HelloWorld' and 'java HelloWorld.class'?
items.a: java HelloWorld is CORRECT — you pass the class name (without extension) to the java command. The JVM looks for HelloWorld.class on the classpath. java HelloWorld.class is INCORRECT — this would cause an error: 'Could not find or load main class HelloWorld.class'. The java command takes a class name, not a filename. Never include the .class extension when running java.

items.q: 7. You get 'UnsupportedClassVersionError' when running a .jar file. What does this mean and how do you fix it?
items.a: UnsupportedClassVersionError means the .jar was compiled with a newer Java version than the JVM you are using to run it. For example, the .jar was compiled with Java 21 but you are running it with Java 11. Fix: Update your JVM to a version equal to or newer than the compile-time version. Run java -version to check current version. Download and install Java 21 and update PATH/JAVA_HOME accordingly.

items.q: 8. What is the advantage of using IntelliJ IDEA over just a text editor + command line for Java development?
items.a: IntelliJ IDEA provides: (1) Smart autocomplete — suggests method names, variables, and API calls. (2) Real-time error detection — highlights compile errors as you type, before running. (3) Built-in debugger — set breakpoints and inspect variable values. (4) Refactoring tools — safely rename variables, extract methods, reorganize code. (5) Integrated Maven/Gradle — manage dependencies without command line. (6) Version control — built-in Git UI. All of this dramatically increases productivity compared to a text editor + terminal.
